author: Dracoblack
quote:
Sometimes, all you need is a small indie game with a genuinely original idea to have more fun than with the biggest AAA productions.
Probably Stolen takes inspiration from games like Papers, Please and puts its own spin on the concept: running a gritty cyberpunk shop in a world that feels dirty, dangerous and wonderfully unconventional. And I mean gritty in the best possible way!
The gameplay loop is deceptively simple but incredibly addictive. You start with basic activities, and the game gradually introduces new mechanics, giving you more responsibilities and opportunities without overwhelming you with endless tutorials. Instead, you get actual printed manuals, sometimes even requiring you to purchase them in game, to learn things like water purification. It makes discovering new mechanics feel rewarding rather than being spoon fed everything like an idiot.
There's a surprising variety of activities. You can collect garbage, work as a chemist, become a winemaker, raise rats or fish for meat, grow vegetables, smuggle goods, trade water and much more. The different professions and their associated perks also change how you approach the beginning of the game. Each offers its own advantages and disadvantages, and although you can eventually unlock other professions by purchasing the necessary equipment, your initial choices genuinely matter.
The perk system is another great addition, offering different ways to approach the game and making progression more interesting. I particularly enjoyed evaluating the items customers bring in, although I wish there were more categories than just three: bionic hands, sandwiches (I love the ribwich lol) and energy cells. 
Hopefully, this system will expand in future updates.
There are also a handful of NPCs with interesting little stories, but unfortunately, there aren't nearly enough of them. It's a shame because the setting has plenty of potential for more memorable characters and interactions.
Overall, Probably Stolen does what it sets out to do extremely well. 
It's an incredibly engaging experience that can easily keep you playing for dozens of hours without feeling repetitive.
And here's the best part: 15 € for almost 80 hours of entertainment (took me that long to take a break), with even more free updates planned, including additional professions and items. That's fantastic value for money, and I genuinely look forward to seeing how much further the developers can expand this little gem. 
A fantastic little indie that proves you don't need a €100 price tag or a massive AAA studio to deliver an incredibly enjoyable experience.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
GTA VI feels less like a Grand Theft Auto game and more like a badly disguised life simulator. At times, I genuinely wondered whether I was playing The Sims instead. Let's start with the gameplay. Apparently, after waiting 13 years, what players really wanted was to spend hours doing household chores. Fixing roofs, painting walls and performing mundane activities... seriously? More than six hours of this nonsense before you're finally allowed to experience something resembling the freedom that made GTA famous. I bought Grand Theft Auto, not a home improvement simulator!And where the hell did Rockstar's sense of humour go? The franchise was famous for outrageous satire, controversial jokes and making fun of absolutely everyone. Now all the sharp edges have been removed, replaced by corporate sensitivity and politically correct writing. The satire is practically dead, and it's hardly surprising considering the feminist driven creative direction. Apparently, being funny and offensive is no longer part of the GTA formula.
Then there's Jason, one of the most disappointing protagonists in the franchise. The poor bastard spends most of his time trying to please Lucia, incapable of doing anything other than being her obedient boyfriend. He can't visit prostitutes, pursue other relationships (exuding getting it from behind by his friend...) or even make his own decisions without worrying about upsetting Lucia. Meanwhile she seems to enjoy considerably more freedom, including being unfaithful. What is this supposed to be, a crime simulator or a masterclass in being a doormat? You're also expected to be nice and accommodating towards practically everyone, including characters representing particular political causes. Your decisions are constantly tracked and supposedly influence the ending. Even reloading a previous save won't necessarily save you from the consequences. Instead of letting players experiment, Rockstar seems determined to judge their behavior. Since when did GTA become a morality examination?
The censorship is another disappointment. GTA has always been about freedom, chaos and pushing boundaries. You can commit violence and murder against plenty of NPCs, but certain politically protected characters and activists apparently enjoy a different set of rules. What happened to the franchise that didn't give a damn about offending people?And then there's the technical disaster. What an absolute clown fiesta! The amount of bugs is ridiculous, including issues serious enough to break gameplay. In my experience, it's worse than Cyberpunk 2077 infamous launch. Naturally, fanboys are already working overtime to justify everything. Apparently, no bug is too serious when it's happening in their beloved GTA.Performance isn't much better. 30 FPS in 2026 is already disappointing, but frequent drops towards 20 FPS are simply unacceptable. We're talking about Rockstar Games, not some tiny independent studio struggling with its first open-world let's talk about the reviews. An absurd number of 100/100 scores, even when the reviews themselves acknowledge significant problems with pacing, mechanics, combat and performance. Really? A perfect score despite all these shortcomings? Some of these reviews read more like marketing material than independent criticism.
Finally, the real Grand Theft Auto experience might actually be the price tag. Multiple editions, increasingly expensive packages and premium pricing for a product packed with questionable design decisions. Apparently, the biggest crime Rockstar wants to commit is against your open-world game should give players freedom, not constantly tell them how to behave. GTA should be outrageous, unpredictable, funny and offensive. That's what made the franchise special.

After 13 years of waiting, I got a glorified household simulator with a toxic relationship, questionable performance, endless bugs and a morality system nobody asked for.Congratulations, Rockstar. 
You managed to make a game about criminals feel like doing your taxes.

author: Dracoblack
quote: In my opinion, Crimson Desert is a true masterpiece. I haven't had this much fun with a game since the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. Crimson Desert doesn't insult your intelligence. It features puzzles, mysteries, and deep lore, all combined with amazing gameplay. And speaking of gameplay, the game doesn't hold your hand or explain every little detail. By combining basic moves, you can pull off some truly epic combos. The story is interesting and features some epic moments. You also get to play as three different characters, each with their own storylines that gradually intertwine, adding even more depth to the overall narrative. However, Crimson Desert isn't a traditional RPG like The Witcher 3, which focuses primarily on storytelling. Instead, Crimson Desert wants to give you freedom. It offers hundreds of missions, countless places to explore, different mounts, beautiful items, and incredibly detailed NPCs. Young or old, male or female, they all look fantastic none of that generic, low-quality character design we've become so accustomed to in modern games. With its latest expansions, the developers have even added an entirely new experience featuring customizable ships and underwater adventures. I honestly can't praise this game enough.Pearl Abyss has achieved in just a few months what other studios take years to accomplish!

author: Dracoblack
quote: Updated my review after years, in 2026 I feel like it can be a 5/10 game, it has a great community, the single player content is now interesting, but the game it is what it is, worth grabbing it for a couple of bucks when on sale, not worth paying a monthly fee and the inventory is not very big for the free versions so I can't say I promote it.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
Already 40 hours into the game and just scratched the surface. Playing on pc, with a mid-end pc and the game is very optimized it runs on ultra settings as default. (I'll talk bugs later)

The story it's just great, not just the main one, but the side ones too. Driving it's a lot of fun and I'm not a car games fan, so it's shooting. Night City it's incredible and really feels like a real city.

Now, about the bugs, who playied the witcher 3 already knows CDPR will provide to fix all the bugs and make the game perfect, if I have to give a bad score for some launch bugs, I'll never had playied Bethesda games, loosing a change to enjoy some of the best games ever made. Cyberpunk at it's core it's great, mechanics and story (and you can't fix them if broken), the bugs will go.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
For me, almost a 10. It has great graphic, great music and sound, great acting voices (played in English) and a very good story. It really feels like the far west, and after 330 hours sincked in the game (100 in the online part) I feel like suggesting this game for the single player. The story is very good, even for people that didn't playied the first game (like me).
The bad about this game it's that some actions are really really slow...especially when in the camp, everything take a lot to do, sit, walk, drink a coffè ecc. I understand they wanted it to be realistic but it's too much, even when looting there is an animation for every item picked up in the chests, drawers ecc. good thing is the action and shooting parts are not slow, and very well made.
And now the bad part, the online it's a buggy mess, full of cheaters, trolls and people that make theyr fun ruining the fun of others. Sometimes there are good players too, but this game has a very bad online community. The worst thing of all it's Rockstar don't care so much about this game, getting rarely updates (the online story mode it's incomplete...), the released updates are nothing new or interesting. at least if you play it often you can have the good things without paying.

So, almost a perfect game, with an online mode to don't look at. The boring slow actions are not something so bad but they are really annoying after playing it for a lot of hours.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
For me this is a small indie pearl, the graphic isn't really something that gets people interested, it has the right mood for the game. What really makes this game shine it's his addiction! Once you start if you love 2D games and the survival genre this game will provide a good amount of fun.
I give only 7 because I think it's a good game, with a lot of fun mechanics, but once you get how they work it becomes easy. Also, the expedition events are not so much so after a while you get used to what will happen.
They did a good job adding some scenarios, custom stories, and there is also the free endless mode. Too bad they didn't expanded on it making more of them or adding more events during the expeditions.

author: Dracoblack
quote: A really enjoyable indie game, when I got it was bug free, not encountered even one. The game is like a sequel of the old x-com games, it provides a lot of fun and a great bang for your bucks. It took me 50 hours to finish it, playing without being in a hurry in normal difficulty. It's not perfect and a lot of things can be improved, but for an indie game I think it's very good. I've evn backed the second on kickstarter, I think the team behind it can get it evn better.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
I'm a fan of MH since the PSP, I really love this games. The pc version it's like a dream coming true, fluid combat a lot of new weapons and monsters, a lot of armors. The game also released a lot of free content making this game even longer.
I'm not a multiplayer person, the only exception is MH, there is a great community and the hunts in party are great.
I've already sink 500 in it, with the Iceborne (paid) expansion and I still have things to do. Great to play for a long time or just as a quick hunt, I always return to this title.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
This vote is not for the "gay" content, it's not like we fans care for sexuality of the characters. We care for the story, and this story is bad, and even worse is the narration, the motivation and the execution of all this story. It's a mess, it's not even a chapter 2 for me, just a bad fan fiction.

Zero is the vote and the money this game and Naughty Dog will get from me in the future. I regret wasting so many hours until the end, just to see how bad it can get.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
A true and rare masterpiece. A lot of content and very high quality, great English interpretation of every character. 2 DLCS so big as the main game and for a very honest price. It's a must play for every fantasy fan.

I really love the world and the attention to every detail and also the great music. The sotry is really nice, even in the side quests (and they are a lot and of great quality). I play this game once in a while just for the vibe and the music.

author: Dracoblack
quote:
A small Indie gem in the cyberpunk genre. The game has good music and ejoyable voice acting. I found the story a classic but enjoyable, with different endings too. There are a lot of interesting concepts like the hacking that is not really enjoyable at first, but gets better with some experience and some extra points in the skill.

It's not very long but also not short for and Indie game, I found a perfect balance and it didn't get boring.

The NPG don't have the best AI but they are quite strong especially near the ending of the game so I didn't got bored of killing them.

Atmosphere and art fell are good and is what a cyberpunk fan expect.
